You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The bug occurs because the MultiDirectional class's iterateSimplex method uses an infinite loop (while (true)) without a proper convergence check to break out when the optimization has converged or reached the desired solution. The test case explicitly shows that the method loops forever if the optimization starts exactly at the correct solution. This is because the iterateSimplex method performs steps like reflection, expansion, and contraction on the simplex vertices but lacks a convergence criterion inside the loop body that allows it to exit once the solution is found or sufficiently improved.

Inspecting the iterateSimplex code snippet:
- The method starts an infinite while(true) loop.
- The iteration counter is incremented for every loop, which can throw an exception when max iterations are exceeded.
- It saves the current simplex and starts with reflection of simplex vertices.
- It checks if the reflected vertex is better than the best, and either expands or accepts the reflected simplex and returns early.
- Otherwise, it attempts contraction and returns early if contracted is better.
- However, if the reflected vertex is not better and the contracted vertex is not better, the loop does not break or return, causing infinite looping.
- There's a commented placeholder "check convergence" but it is never executed because the loop condition is always true and no convergence criteria is implemented.

The current bug report confirms this by stating "MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex loops forever if the starting point is the correct solution" and the test case tries to optimize starting at the maximum location, causing the infinite loop.

In summary, the root cause is that iterateSimplex lacks a proper convergence check inside the infinite loop to stop iterating when the solution has converged, especially in the case where the starting point is already optimal.

The related methods involved include:
- iterateSimplex: the main loop with missing convergence check.
- incrementIterationsCounter: limits iterations but does not prevent infinite loop before max iterations.
- evaluateNewSimplex and evaluateSimplex: these handle creating and evaluating new simplex points correctly.

The fix should add a convergence check based on the simplex points or the progress made in iterateSimplex so the infinite loop can break and not continue forever when the solution is already known or optimal.

The test case clearly demonstrates the failure scenario, and the code confirms the while(true) loop without convergence is the cause. This matches the report's description precisely. Other recent bug reports do not relate directly to this issue.

Suggested methods for fix location:
- MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex(java.util.Comparator<org.apache.commons.math.optimization.RealPointValuePair>)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
